method.heading: CMAP Method
method.summary: CMAP constructs an action tape from executed-action history and future action positions. It predicts a coarse future chunk and per-step span-selection scores, selects the contiguous window with the highest mean score, and regenerates only that interval while preserving coarse predictions outside it. Selection and regeneration can repeat for multiple passes before receding-horizon execution.

stages.title: Predict
stages.description: The current observation and visible executed-action history condition a coarse prediction of future actions and per-step span-selection scores.

stages.title: Select
stages.description: Contiguous future windows are ranked by their mean scores. The first maximizing window defines the selected span, and positions regenerated in earlier passes are excluded from later selections.

stages.title: Regenerate
stages.description: The local refiner regenerates only the selected span and merges it with preserved coarse actions. After the configured passes, the completed tape is executed with receding-horizon control.

simulation.heading: Simulation Experiments
simulation.summary: We evaluate CMAP on eight RoboTwin tasks and three single-arm ManiSkill tasks, using 50 and 100 expert demonstrations per task, respectively. ACT, DP, and CMAP are each evaluated over 100 episodes per RoboTwin task.

real_world.heading: Real-World Experiments
real_world.summary: We evaluate ACT, DP, and CMAP on the AGIBOT G1 and Leju Kuavo 4 Pro platforms. Together, these physical deployments expose the policies to contact dynamics, arm-hand coordination, sensing noise, control latency, and communication delay.

platforms.title: Long-horizon dexterous manipulation
platforms.description: The Kuavo setup controls one 7-DoF arm equipped with a dexterous hand from synchronized multi-view RGB observations at 10 Hz.

platforms.title: Contact-rich tabletop manipulation
platforms.description: The AGIBOT setup controls the right 7-DoF arm and scalar gripper from head- and right-wrist-camera RGB streams, with a 15-Hz policy loop and a 100-Hz low-level arm-control loop.

table.title: Real-world success counts and rates
table.note: Chess Grasp and Bottle Grasp are checkpoints within 10 shared Dual-Item Placement trials; Outcome Avg. aggregates five outcomes.

real_world.protocol: Each task uses 50 teleoperated demonstrations shared across ACT, DP, and CMAP. Synchronized RGB, proprioception, commands, and timestamps are recorded, and each method is evaluated over 10 matched physical trials per task. Outcomes are verified from video and logs, with joint and workspace limits, joint-delta clipping, emergency stops, and home-reset procedures enforced throughout evaluation.

ablations.heading: Ablations
ablations.summary: Matched configurations distinguish the contributions of executed-action history, contiguous masked regeneration, and score-guided span selection on the fixed RoboTwin diagnostic suite and ManiSkill.

ablations.detail: Per prediction cycle, CMAP regenerates one 8-action span within a 50-step RoboTwin chunk and one 8-action span within a 30-step ManiSkill chunk. The reported deployment configuration uses one regeneration pass; RoboTwin also enables temporal aggregation with per-step replanning.

success_failure.heading: Success and Failure Cases
success_failure.summary: Physical execution pairs on AGIBOT G1 and Kuavo 4 Pro isolate four contact failures and one recovered near-failure. Successful examples establish centered contact and maintain object alignment; the remaining difficult cases concentrate around contact geometry, grasp closure, object alignment, and sustained support.

cases.description: The gripper enters the cup opening without establishing stable rim contact, preventing clean separation.
Off-center contact redirects the applied force and fails to fully depress the button.
The chess-piece grasp misses a stable opposing contact.
The bottle is acquired at a tilted pose that can cause slip or collision before placement.
The sheet briefly relies on unstable single-point support, but the policy recovers the transport and placement sequence.

success_failure.extension: The current policy has no direct tactile or force measurements. The remaining failures motivate contact-sensitive span-selection scores and a recovery controller that can reopen a new interval when the expected contact event is absent.

title: CMAP: Continuous Masked Action-Tape Modeling for Visuomotor Manipulation
abstract: Action-chunking policies generate temporally coherent action sequences but usually treat a predicted chunk as a monolithic output, so a short contact or alignment error can compromise an otherwise valid motion. We propose CMAP, a history-conditioned continuous masked action policy that treats each chunk as an editable prediction. CMAP combines recent executed commands and future action positions in a continuous action tape. Given visual observations, robot proprioception, and executed-action history, a coarse decoder predicts a K-step future chunk and span-selection scores. A max-mean rule selects a high-scoring contiguous interval, and a local refiner regenerates the selected interval while preserving coarse actions outside it. The merged chunk is executed with receding-horizon control, repeatedly anchoring future prediction to commands already issued by the robot. CMAP averages 63.9% on eight RoboTwin tasks, compared with 45.8% for ACT and 34.8% for Diffusion Policy, and reaches 53.3% on ManiSkill versus 26.0% for ACT. Across AGIBOT G1 and Leju Kuavo 4 Pro evaluations, CMAP completes 38 of 50 outcomes, compared with 25 for ACT and 24 for Diffusion Policy. These results demonstrate consistent gains from history-conditioned local regeneration in simulated and physical visuomotor manipulation.
